args.name: Assess and recover usable bark
args.function: Determine whether accessible fallen woody material actually carries recoverable bark, and, if suitable material exists, learn a manual method to separate usable roofing bark without creating material or treating every branch as suitable.
args.conditions: Shared-shelter construction requires bark. Nearby fallen branches are observed, but their bark content, suitability and separability are unknown. No bark source has yet been located in my personal observations.
args.inputs: Actual accessible bark-bearing fallen material, if present; any necessary tools or other inputs remain unknown.
args.costs: Unknown study time, work, energy and material losses; establish these before use.
args.effects: Enable evidence-based assessment and, only where physically applicable, transfer existing bark into usable owned material while accounting for the remaining wood. No shelter or bark is presumed produced by this request.

candidates.function: Build a low single-person braced lean-to with a sloping bark roof from owned branches, vines and bark at a clear site; inspect, repair or dismantle it, or resume or cancel unfinished work.
candidates.costs: Study: 4 rounds. Start: x, y, orientation (degrees; 0 points the low roof edge toward increasing x, where wind comes from) and materials as exact owned, untreated whole units totalling 13 branch, 4 vine and 6 bark; stand within reach of a 2 m x 2 m footprint of ordinary dry soil that is inside the world, unobstructed and unoccupied. Twelve paid increments, one round and 1 energy each: 2 posts, 3 ridge and braces, 3 ribs and binding, 3 roofing courses, 1 final check; start pays the first and the same action continues each round. Resume pays the next increment of the unfinished work; cancel takes one round and no energy. Inspect: target in reach, one round, 0.2 energy. Repair (builder only): target, increment 1-11 and the exact replacement units of that increment, one round, 1 energy. Dismantle (builder only): target, one round and 1 energy per stage, removing the last installed stage. Gathering, travel and probe tests are separate actions with their own costs.
candidates.effects: Reserved materials stay carried and owned until each paid increment moves them into the structure as installed parts with the same quantity, origin and age; nothing is created or used up. After the final stability, binding, roof-load and runoff checks the shelter is commissioned: a 2 m x 1 m covered floor under a 1.2 m ridge and a roof sloping about 50 degrees. While exactly one person lies wholly on that floor in rain and wind up to 0.8, it removes up to 50% of the rain part and up to 35% of the wind part of the existing outdoor exposure chill, scaled by roof condition, by the share of the body under the roof along the wind-driven rain, and for wind by how directly the low edge faces the wind; wind entering the open side, stronger weather, water pooling on the floor or a second person gives no protection. Air temperature, hunger, nutrition and rest are unchanged, and copies never stack. A frame without its three roofing courses gives no rain protection. Each round installed parts wear by 0.0005 + 0.002 x rain + 0.002 x wind; a part below condition 0.5 makes a commissioned shelter unsafe with no protection until repair and a passing reinspection. Repair restores only the replaced parts; removed and dismantled parts return to the ground at the site with their condition and can be reused at that condition. Work not continued in a round pauses; a lost reserved material stops it. Cancel returns uninstalled materials once and leaves installed parts as an unfinished structure; death stops the work, drops uninstalled materials where the person died and leaves installed parts. No reward, mastery or refund.

candidates.function: Build two to four adjacent, independently braced lean-to bays reached from one shared open side, from owned branches, vines and bark at a clear site; each bay shelters one person. Inspect, repair or dismantle bays, or resume or cancel unfinished work.
candidates.costs: Study: 4 rounds. Start: x, y (the centre of the whole footprint), orientation (degrees; 0 points every low roof edge toward increasing x, where wind comes from, and the shared open side toward decreasing x), bays (2-4, default 2) and materials as exact owned, untreated whole units totalling 13 branch, 4 vine and 6 bark per bay (26, 8 and 12 for two bays); stone is not accepted. The footprint is 2 m across by 2 m per bay along the ridge, of ordinary dry soil, inside the world, unobstructed and unoccupied, and you stand within reach of the first bay; a 1 m strip along the open side must be walkable, inside the world and free of solid objects. Twelve paid increments per bay, one round and 1 energy each (24 rounds and 24 energy for two bays), bay after bay: 2 posts, 3 ridge and braces, 3 ribs and binding, 3 roofing courses, 1 final check; start pays the first and the same action continues each round; each increment needs reach to the bay being built. Resume pays the next increment of the unfinished work; cancel takes one round and no energy. Inspect: a bay in reach as target, one round, 0.2 energy, covering every bay of the structure in reach. Repair (builder only): target bay, increment 1-11 and the exact replacement units of that increment, one round, 1 energy. Dismantle (builder only): target bay, one round and 1 energy per stage, removing that bay's last installed stage. Gathering, travel, messages and probe tests are separate actions with their own costs.
candidates.effects: Reserved materials stay carried and owned until each paid increment moves them into its bay as installed parts with the same quantity, origin and age; nothing is created or used up. Each bay is a full braced lean-to with its own posts and braces (no spanning roof or shared members) and its own 2 m x 1 m covered floor under a 1.2 m ridge. A bay's final stability, binding, roof-load, runoff and open-approach checks commission that bay alone. While exactly one person lies wholly on a commissioned bay's floor in rain and wind up to 0.8, that bay removes up to 50% of the rain part and up to 35% of the wind part of the existing outdoor exposure chill, scaled by its roof condition, by the share of the body under its roof along the wind-driven rain, and for wind by how directly its low edge faces the wind; people on other bays do not change it, but two people on the same bay floor, wind into the open side, stronger weather or water pooling on the floor give that bay no protection. Air temperature, hunger, nutrition and rest are unchanged, and shelters never stack. Each round every installed part wears by 0.0005 + 0.002 x rain + 0.002 x wind; a part below condition 0.5 makes that bay unsafe with no protection until repair and a passing reinspection. Changes in who lies on each bay floor are reported. Repair restores only the replaced parts; removed and dismantled parts return to the ground at the bay with their condition and can be reused. Work not continued in a round pauses; a lost reserved material stops it. Cancel returns uninstalled materials once, leaves partly built bays unfinished and keeps commissioned bays; death stops the work, drops uninstalled materials where the person died and leaves installed parts. Nobody else is moved, helped or given access; each person acts and pays for themselves. No reward, mastery or refund.

response.text: {"queries":[],"result_json":"{\"reviews\":[{\"actor\":\"ivo\",\"decision\":\"develop\",\"ability\":null,\"reason\":\"The completed related-capability search found observation and limited sample tests, gathering, and shelter assembly, but no equivalent bark-separation operation. probe (open-baseline:probe:1, handler open.probe, foundation-open@1) can observe a visible target; its press/wet/heat modes do not implement peeling or recover roofing sheets. gather transfers existing loose stock and cannot convert unspecified branches into bark. Develop a general assessment-and-manual-separation operation, reusing existing observation and inventory machinery. The two owned branches are possible assessment targets, not verified bark-bearing inputs. Missing physical representation belongs in the current development handoff, not a claim that bark exists or a permanent rejection.\",\"specification\":\"Develop 'Assess and manually separate bark', parameterized by exact target reference, mode (inspect, separation-trial, recover, resume, cancel), selected surface region or quantity, and optional exact tool references. Applicable to accessible fallen woody material generally, not just Ivo's branches. Inspect requires visibility and interaction reach; destructive trials and recovery require owned material within reach, or independently established lawful access under existing rules. No living-tree felling, automatic collection, invented tools, or implied permission. Exact candidate references are item-57-ivo-603 (2 branch units, owned by ivo, originating at canopy-26), start-0-branches, start-1-branches and canopy-74. These are candidates only: natural-source stock is not owned work material. canopy-26 and forest-branch-0 are currently exhausted; the tick-55 observation of canopy-26 does not override its later state. Do not target the unrelated root item.\\nDependencies and reuse: record reuse of open.probe's observe implementation and visible-target resolution, plus existing ownership, stock-transfer, work-state and event machinery actually available in the handoff. Inspection through this interface must not add a second observation charge. Retain gather for separate collection of genuinely available loose stock. Existing simple-shelter and shared-shelter consume bark; neither supplies extraction or proves that a recovered piece meets its input contract.\\nPhysical prerequisite: the handoff must support an authoritative material record with actual bark presence, attached bark quantity, wood quantity, condition, accessible geometry, sheet dimensions and measured separability, including an unknown state. A generic branch quantity alone is insufficient evidence. Inspect can reveal only visible surface facts; a paid trial can reveal local separation behavior and damage. Do not backfill existing branch items with a favorable bark fraction. Where the world lacks a physically supported composition or measurement mechanism, implement that missing mechanism in this same handoff. The smallest executable precursor is honest visible assessment with an explicit unresolved-composition result; recovery remains unavailable on an unresolved target, not permanently rejected. No remote search, hidden-resource locations or unobserved internal quantities are disclosed.\\nCosts and progress: learning takes 2 study rounds individually, using the existing study rules, without material grants. Development/review waiting advances no simulation time. Inspect costs 1 active round and 0.2 energy, with no material consumption. A separation trial costs 1 active round and 0.5 energy on at most 0.1 actual input unit; the selected portion must exist and be exclusively reserved before work. It may damage that portion but does not automatically destroy all of it. Recovery is hand-only where a trial demonstrates an accessible peelable edge and separation possible at safe manual force. Otherwise report the missing edge/tool or unsuitable material; do not assume a knife. Process at most 0.1 square metre of measured accessible bark surface per increment, costing 1 active round and 1 energy per increment, including a smaller final increment. Harder material that cannot separate under this bounded operation is not silently processed more quickly. Tool-assisted cutting is outside this minimal version until an actual applicable tool and its use mechanism are established. Each increment checks reach, ownership/access, remaining energy, target condition, available edge and available unprocessed surface before paying and acting. No queued increment progresses while paused. Travel, gathering, and communication are separate paid actions.\\nConservation and products: lock only the selected actual portion, never the entire source unnecessarily. Each completed increment transfers existing attached bark to detached sheets, fragments or waste and leaves the residual wood and remaining attached bark explicitly represented. Preserve origin, age and condition; track newly caused tears and damage. Account for parent quantity by an authoritative component ledger: residual wood plus remaining attached bark plus recovered pieces plus recorded waste must equal the processed input on the same material basis. Do not retain two full branch units while also granting additional unaccounted bark. Measured area and dimensions describe products but cannot be substituted for conserved material quantity. Do not invent a fixed branch-to-bark conversion. Integration must establish the existing inventory-unit/component mapping before granting quantity-bearing outputs. If that mapping is not yet executable, the assessment/trial precursor reports findings without granting stock.\\nA detached piece is roofing-suitable only after actual evidence of continuous coverage, dimensions, flexibility and condition satisfies the receiving shelter's implemented material validation. Record those measured properties on the product. Register any necessary compatible bark-unit conversion explicitly in the handoff and test it against the existing shelter contracts; do not change their 6-bark-per-bay requirement or label fragments as roofing units. Until compatibility is established, recovered material is a measured bark sheet or fragment, not certified shelter input. No shelter, weather protection, nutrition or stock regeneration follows from extraction alone.\\nInterruption: apply completed increments atomically with a durable work identifier and consumed/remaining-region ledger. Interruption before an increment commits leaves that increment unpaid and unprocessed. Loss of reach, material, access, energy or safe conditions pauses work with its reason. Resume revalidates conditions and operates only on the remainder, paying normal costs. Cancel costs 1 round and no energy, releases reservations, and leaves all completed products, damage and residual material in their actual state. Death stops work and releases reservations; carried inputs and products follow existing death/drop rules. Completed time, energy and material damage are never refunded; uncommitted debits are rolled back exactly once. No duplicated outputs on retries. There is no unattended extraction process. Products and residual material retain existing decay rules without resetting age; storage, later damage and any actual maintenance use existing rules. Do not invent maintenance benefits or a recurring production stream. All applicability, conservation, work progression and validation rules execute in code rather than recurring model review.\",\"learning\":2,\"experienceReview\":\"No pleasure or maintained satisfaction for requesting, reviewing, learning, querying, naming or registering this operation. A committed inspection or physical trial may qualify as verified information gain only for new, personally applicable evidence, including an informative failed peel; an unresolved or unmeasured conclusion does not qualify. Deduplicate by actor, material provenance, tested region, property and materially unchanged conditions, including equivalent probe observations. Use existing coded experience rules if applicable. If no compatible rule exists, award zero pending implementation rather than inventing account changes. Any later experiential rule needs an explicit bounded amount and cap, cooldown and decay before activation. Legitimate repeated manual practice may support only the existing modest sustained-benefit rules; novelty is not required and repeated identical evidence is not repeated discovery. Do not alter protected rewards, budgets, goals, permissions or basic nutrition. No comfort benefit is produced by detached bark; any later physical comfort remains capped at 10 and requires actual shelter use.\",\"visualReview\":\"Emit observable inspection, trial-started, trial-failed, separation-progress, material-detached, paused, resumed and cancelled events only when those actions occur. Persist reusable visual metadata on the work target and actual products: target/product IDs, provenance, inspected or processed region, visible attached/peeled area, measured sheet outline and dimensions, condition, damage, remaining work and evidence references. Render unknown composition as unknown, not as an exposed bark reserve. Distinguish unsuitable, unresolved, incomplete and verified-separated states. Show peeled surfaces and detached pieces only after committed physical changes; show roofing suitability only after its validation passes. Inspection, a failed trial, development and learning cannot display successful bark production or a completed roof. Other participants receive only observations or communications they actually encounter and must communicate and act independently.\"}]}"}
